q.4491: Brakmar is trying to take control of the Bay of Cania and the Dopple Territory so as to block access to the port and pillage the maritime traffic in the area. I've already sent a patrol there and I'd like you to throw your weight behind them. When the battle is over, report to Justfa Lafs and come back here.
q.5190:
I don't need anything from you right now. 
Go back and see the chief of your militia.
q.4506: You managed it!? You found a competent tactician? I'd like to believe that Justfa was in seventh heaven. This tactician helped us apply our strategies and to communicate with our men better than ever.
q.4549: I already know, a parcel from Astrub has just arrived. Just after your defeat, the Astrub mercenaries intervened because of the ruckus caused by the fight and they arrested the Brakmarians. Magus Ax retrieved the Fogornleg Horn and sent it to us, saying that you refused to give it to the Brakmarians and were prepared to die defending it. When I think of all the trouble we've gone through to obtain this horn... It will teach us not to put our faith in rumours and legends. If it's any consolation, there will be fewer young recruits on potato peeling duty thanks to the power of this Horn. You have served Bonta brilliantly and your loyalty is worth more to me than some magic object.
q.9907: Hey, now! Don't get too excited! You've achieved a great feat, to be sure, but there's one last step you have to complete for all that to be realised.
q.4550: Ahh, so that's why Danathor wanted to speak with you... Thanks for telling me, but alas, it's useless. Your testimony is worthless considering the support he has from his high-placed friends. The best thing to do is to find the thief he hired.
q.4554:
Ah, that's horrible. Get that handkerchief away from me, there's no way I'm touching that filthy thing. It's bad enough to look at, but the smell... as though it's been used to whip... unruly slave-fish or some such horror. 
Listen to me carefully now, here's what you do: make a fire, and burn that godforsaken thing. Then heat water on the fire, and draw yourself a good, hot bath. Finally, and most importantly, chew on a hot coal for a while to get rid of that bad breath of yours.
q.4567: Hello, how do you fancy a change of scenery? I've got just the thing for you. Head over to Moon Island and find the guardian of the Fogornleg Horn. If you can recover the Fogornleg Horn at the same time, so much the better.
q.4581: Hello, more haste, less speed. we haven't been able to flatter Elturt, but as she doesn't seem too belligerent there must be some way of sorting something out with her to obtain the Fogornleg Horn. We need to get to know her better, which means getting the advice of an animal specialist. There are several in Sufokia but the best suited would be Oshimo, I think. He's responsible for the Kennel to the north of Sufokia. Make your investigations as subtle as possible, rushing things won't work there either.
q.9961:
Were you sent by the Astrubian Mercenaries? And with everything you need! Haha, you're saving my bacon.

This is just what I needed. Thanks to you, I'll finally be able to advance.

Here, take this as a reward. You've earned it.
q.4583:
You look a bit too pale to be a member of the Brakmarian Militia. Have you swallowed a Kralove the wrong way, by any chance?
Ah, you've brought me the documents that the Bontarian stole, but there should be three of you, no? I suppose the two others stopped off at the inn. Go and join them, I'll pass these documents on to Kaffra Keeper as soon as he comes out of his meditation.
q.4612: What news have you brought me?
q.4729:
The hilt of the sword is made of wood, but not just any old wood. Hornbeam Wood bewitched by dark magic is needed, but I don't know how to do all this.
Search the lumberjacks' workshops and find somone who does.
q.4619: And you wish to learn how to use it? Join me in the basement of the Alchemists' Market and we'll carry out the Revelation Ritual. In a corner is a cupboard. Stand in front of this cupboard and follow the passage that will open up before you. You'll need to bring two trusted friends with you, I want to help but I don't want to do your work for you. I'll make a list of the items you'll need. Bring them with you and everything should go well, unless you replace the Magical Cure for a Sulphur Pouch. It's very important you don't have any sulphur in your inventory, understood?
q.4660: The documents that you recovered from our spy reveal the location of the Primordial Cauldron which, according to legend, could cook enough food in less than a day to satisfy even the appetite of dragons at their unique banquet. I'm surprised the cauldron is in the woods, it must be well hidden and difficult to get to. Go over the place with a fine-tooth comb, the documents are quite clear about the location. As for the documents that the Bontarians tried to steal from us, they list the necessary ingredients to prepare an irresistible dish for Elturt. As I'm sure you'll agree, I think we'll need more than the back-scratcher to coax that evil turtle out of its shell.
q.4667:
What? Did I really just hear what I think I heard? You stupid idiot! You stinking piece of Ouassingue turd!
Get out of my sight before I kill you!
q.4674:
A Brakmarian! But how did you know the location of the Horn?
Whatever, I'll send you back where you came from! En garde!
q.4694: Sorry to bother you with this, but a friend of mine, a militiaman called Kit Dingaround, is under suspicion of having betrayed Bonta for a bribe... that's why he was thrown in jail like a common criminal. He's a great kid and would never even think of doing such a thing. I'm convinced that it's a plot against him! Go see Kit in prison and try to clear the story up.
q.4746:
A delay in the treason case? Hmm, hmmm... *hic*
I hate investigations that drag on, but since you seem like a decent chap, I'll do what you *hic* ask in exchange for a little favour from you.
I need alcohol to make the prisoners talk but the reserves have run out. *hic* I need a barrel of Shambrosia to continue with the questioning, only Gordo McRamsay in Amakna knows the secret. Oh, and while you're here, I'm looking for an Astrub woman too, but marriage agencies aren't what they used to be. It would be great if you could handle it instead.
q.4753: What? You gave the burglars a thumping and then you managed to convince them in their hideout to come and join the militia? Excellent Brakmarian reflexes! Never forget that the more deceitful people are, the more likely they're to be useful to us eventually.
q.9975: We don't put up with slackers or fools around here. Any mercenary worth their salt can assess the risks and succeed in their mission.
q.4756:
Merlanmagus sent you? Well in that case, I'll tell you what you need to do. I've prepared things for you, all you need to find are some farmers, alchemists, a little potion and the spell. 
The farmers stand on the white marks... and make sure they're able to grow oats, or they may ruin everything. The alchemists stand on the black marks and they must be able to use Freyesque Orchids in their potions. If you're an alchemist or a farmer yourself, you can stand on either the black or white mark. If not, just let me know when everyone's in their place.
q.4761: Thanks a lot. I'll read these letters later *hic*. I'll give you some more time for your investigation. Don't *hic* worry.
q.4797:
A Sram? That is interesting. We must find him at all costs!
Speaking of fish, Kook Fech has just prepared some for the militia, I've put some aside for you.
q.4902:
Let me take a look.
Well, it says that you need a piece of wood torn from the backside of a Dark Treechnid. It must be carved according to the instructions herein so that its magic will open the passage leading to the Hammer of Light. It also states that many people must work together to open the gate that holds the vampire prisoner.
The crypt is located underground in the Amakna Cemetery.
I think you know everything now, so find a carver able to carve the piece of wood torn from a Dark Treechnid, and ask your companions to help you open the crypt and defeat the vampire.
q.4911: Did Ebru Of El send you? I have to be honest and tell you that my research was fruitless. I have, on the other hand, heard of a medium capable of entering into contact with souls. She disappeared without trace a decade ago and her family remained discreet about the circumstances of this sudden disappearance. However, Xeloro Verpowered knew her well enough and might be able to tell you something. If she's in town, she'll be south of the arena. She often gets advice about fairyworks from Moob Tsinhcetoryp.
q.4919: You're looking for a Feca doll to comfort a spirit? That's very nice of you. I'm more than happy to make one for you but you'll need to fetch the ingredients. Go get me 30 Flax Fibres for its clothes, 10 Lousy Pig Leathers for wings, 2 White Dreggon Shells for the eyes, 1 Rat Fang for the horns, 30 Boowolf Hair for the hair, 2 Farle's Pig Skins for the tongue, 10 Purple Bwork Leathers for the skin, 5 Plain Boar Leathers for the strap, 4 Prespic Paws for the feet, 3 Furious Trool Wool for stuffing and 30 Flax String to sew it all together.
q.4922: *blushes* It would be a pleasure but I have a lot tiring work to do right now. I promise that we will have another opportunity when I'm not as busy.
q.4973:
What? WHAT?! You dare to criticise my plan? Watch your manner, lowly servant. You'll do as I say, and you'll do it without saying a thing, ok!
If you need help, ask the other idiots in the Tower of Brakmar instead of coming to bother me!
q.4983: IIIIDDDDDDDIIIIIOOOOOOTTTTTT!! What? You want to kill me too? Well I think it's too late for that... a Bontarian is on the case! The medallion? He took it, obviously. I think he went north of here. I gave him one before I kicked the bucket so he won't be going anywhere quick... you should be able to catch him...
q.5468: But you see what makes this story funny is the unseemliness of the situation which brings a bear, plantigrade without the ability to speak, to order a beer in a tavern... unless, of course, it's the fact that you're not even surprised by this setting of the story...
q.5042: Hello, I have another mission for you. As you surely know, there are many mines near Brakmar - Bonta has no such luck. We have to stop Brakmar taking control of these mines, and to do this, we're going to draw the best fighters they have away... Get over there now and visit them all. I want a full report when you return.
q.5125: Can't do a thing, Rogue Inkgo won't say a word. Go and see Merlinmagus Ambrosius at the alchemists workshop and ask him tp prepare some Truth Serum. Then this cursed Rogue will have to confess everything.
q.5134: Huh? The Order of the Sharpened Spatula? That doesn't mean a thing. But I like it! Ok, you got it... I declare the Order of the Sharpened Spatula OPEN! The chief of the order will be the oh-so-powerful As'Ruoy'Dnim.
q.5203:
So, this is the famous Ronan. I had imagined a... bigger man. We'll take care of it right away...
Ah, we'll have to go ask Raaga too. I need to learn some new techniques for brain washing... I think the Goblin should have a few. I think Raaga is in the library.
q.5410:
Come on now, sing with me. 'When you call Bibi, he'll always come running. He's full of life and he's got some left over. All along the Rocky Plains, people are talking. He's always winning...'
Well what do you want to do? You want to leave the dungeon? If you have the key of the Rainbow Blop's Lair, I can take you.
q.5473: Me coming sometime, me like Park. Me like Park and Apples! ... and funny stories also!
q.5489: I saw you challenging Ougaa. You could almost pass for one of my students if you knew how to dress a little better. It hurts my eyes just looking at you. Talk about colour-clash...
q.5544:
Praise be to Silvosse! Praise to the little Dreggon that he taught to fly. I am eternally greatful and I am certain that the Goddess Pandawa has taken notice of your actions. 
I can teach you no more. It's time you take your first steps in Bonta alone.
q.5521:
Ok, let's see now... Stable situation over the last fourteen days... hmmm... The Amakna social services can help you alright. 
You can become an Amaknan once more, but you'll lose your rank in the militia... and all the advantages that come with it.
The administrative costs can be very high according to your reputation and your achievements, so think long and hard before you decide. 
Don't forget! You have to go through each step in the procedure if you want to become Neutral. If you quit before completing the process, you'll lose any money you've spent.
q.5523:
If serving Bonta is your bag, I can arrange the papers to affiliate you to their militia. That'll save me some time and it won't cost you a penny. 
Why am I doing all this, you ask. Well, Bonta gives me a few perks for every new recruit I send their way. 
However, I suggest you go see Snori Nairb in Astrub before you join the alignment, he rewards anyone who wishes to enrol.
q.5534:
Praise be to Silvosse! Praise to the little Dreggon that he taught to fly. I am eternally greatful and I am certain that the God Osamodas has taken notice of your actions. 
I can teach you no more. It's time you take your first steps in Bonta alone.
q.5536:
Praise be to Silvosse! Praise to the little Dreggon that he taught to fly. I am eternally greatful and I am certain that the God Sram has taken notice of your actions. 
I can teach you no more. It's time you take your first steps in Bonta alone.
q.6715: You must be wondering what I'm doing here, no? No, I'm not afraid of Scaraleaves, I came of my own will to meditate. I can leave when I want.
q.5567:
Great! You got here in time to stop the fields being contaminated. I'm very pleased with you. 
I've promoted you to Spy, and something tells me it won't be long before I'll need you again.
Here's 1,000 Kamas for your trouble. By the way, how did it go with Fidji Merline?
q.5574:
Very good. I'm delighted you've become an apprentice of mine. 
Forced resurrection takes a long time to get right, so I won't be needing you for the time being. Go keep an eye on your companions, just as the goddess Jiva keeps an eye on you!
q.5588: Hey, come on, who do you think you're? Have some respect for your elders, you little Gobball pat. Your mother mustn't have given you enough spankings when you were a child, but don't worry, I'll bring it up to date once I get my body back.
q.5647:
Good, I can see You're motivated.
We're going to get our hands on some statues which symbolise the good and evil in humanity. When our task is over, the world will sink into despair, making conquest inevitable. 
Divad Dleifrepok has managed to find out where the statues are located, and you'll go there to take out the guards. You can take some companions with you if you like, that way you won't get bored. 
The statuettes are hidden in an old abandoned mine near the Enutrof temple. Setag blocked up the entrance, but there should be a way to get in nearby. Have a good look around.
q.5652: I don't know what you're talking about. Anyway, that's no way to talk to someone older than you. we haven't exactly raised our Gobballs in the same field, now have we.
q.5704: Noooo!! You stupid idiot! You Gobball intestine! You Bwork horn! You piece of Kralove dung!
q.5723:
It was dark and everyone was asleep except the lookout when a flare bloomed over our heads. We saw small, dark shapes by its light and when it disappeared, Dike Tarak was gone. The whole thing did not last more than ten seconds. The children were immediately escorted to Bonta while a handful of us went in search of Dike Tarak, but without success.
I'll indicate on your map exactly where we were.
q.5725:
Strange, very strange. This is the first time I've been told such a story, excepting the stories of Captain Igloute. Do not tell anyone else. I will immediately tell Justfa so that he can quarantine the area.
In fact, Dike Tarak was not captured by these creatures, but he fled and lost his way. He just returned safely to Bonta.
But back to your promotion. If you want to become Supreme Assassin, you'll have to make your way to Brakmar and ask our spy about Statuette of Sumens that the Brakmarians just recovered.
q.5737:
I expected better from you but I had prepared myself for this eventuality. The statuette that that Brakmarians stole is a fake. The real Statuette is right now hidden away in a safe place under the protection of Jiva.
...
I miss my little piwis. I still remember the time when the city of Bonta had its resurgence. We lacked for young recruits so badly, I put piwis through military training so as not to lose the upper hand. Although those days are long gone, I have decided to train a small commando unit of elite piwis. For this I'll need some sesanabolic seeds, and only Merlinmagus Ambrosius knows their secret. Go ask him about them.
q.5965: Putting up with Djaul is a tough cross to bear.
q.5738:
Bravo, I expected no less from you. Take these few Kamas as a reward for your valour.
...
I miss my little piwis. I still remember the time when the city of Bonta had its resurgence. We lacked for young recruits so badly, I put piwis through military training so as not to lose the upper hand. Although those days are long gone, I have decided to train a small commando unit of elite piwis. For this I'll need some sesanabolic seeds, and only Merlinmagus Ambrosius knows their secret. Go ask him about them.
q.9976: Anyone who wears this helmet has left a mark on our group's story. It's up to you to write the next chapter.
q.5746:
It can cost you anything from 500 to 256,000 Kamas to go neutral. It all depends on how high you've climbed in the ranks of your militia.
What I can do is convert you to the weaker alignment for free. If you're a glory hunter looking to hop on the dominant alignment's bandwagon, well you'll just have to put your hand in your pocket!
q.5789:
Whenever I sneeze, time seems to take a turn for the worse. Rude people claim it's because I once tripped over that brown rug there and accidentally spilt Ouassingue Juice on the hands of Xelor's Clock, but that's not true - I'm just allergic to pollen. I'm doing my best to look after myself, but how am I supposed to stop myself from ever sneezing again?
To make up for all the trouble, I often hand out sweets to the long-suffering inhabitants of Amakna.
They seem to do the trick, and I'm pretty proud of myself because at the moment, everything seems to be OK.

*Rolls her eyes and sniffs noisily*

Oh no, oh...
q.5837:
The protectors of the cities have decided to use the power of Statues of Sumens. Everyone thought they had the two real statuettes, which meant that the real real ones lost their power as soon as they were set free. The protectors then realiised that the statuette they stole from the city was itself only a common copy! The whole world will be upset by this, and you're going to go investigate.

Visit the other order masters and find out their opinion. Then go see Oto Mustam to find out how all this has affected him. After you've done all this, come and report to me.
q.5891: I hope this plan will secure our victory over Bonta.
q.6981: For a Xelor, Xeloro Verpowered wasn't very good at divination. Nevertheless, I remember she once told me about a rare and powerful magic object, able to preserve and restore thoughts and memories. It was called a Wyrmwell. I would gladly have helped more, but I am no expert on dragons. You would be better off contacting the Master of the Osamodas class, he has a reputation for knowing about dragons, like many other followers of the that god.
q.6060: I wonder where Sumens got to. We had planned to head off to the Cania Plains to drink our troubles away... he must have started without me.
q.6092: Many Protectors have no respect for one another, and this Assembly is only pulling them further apart. Nothing good can come of this.
q.6100: Greetings. Such an evil aura cannot pass unfelt. Tell me what I need to know about the Assmembly of Protectors.
q.6106:
Did the Protectors really carry on like you say? You have to wonder who the real bad guys are in this story. 
I think you deserve to join the ranks of the Masters of Shadows.
What do you think of that?
q.6163: I've seen several and have had the chance to study them, uncovering some of their secrets. Sometimes it may seem they're unique, but this is not true. My research tells me that Dragons don't lay a single Dofus, but often entire bundles! Just one of these eggs gives birth to a real Dragon. As for the others, I don't know what becomes of them.
q.6194:
Let me siiiing, let me siiiii.... nnngggg.
Oh hello, I didn't hear you coming. So, tell me, doesn't that big boil in the middle of your face bother you? It's really horrible, you should try covering it up. 
But what am I talking about... I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Pandalida, the famous singer from the first season of the Amakna's Got Talent. I hope you haven't come to get an autograph off me...
q.6209:
If I were you I'd think long and hard about this. Many militiamen patrol these parts - all I've to do is scream and they'll come running. 
If you want some excitement, why don't you go buy one of our charming hostesses a drink.
q.6211:
Have you seen me? What kind of a pole do you take me for?
But wait... Don't you find that it smells of Brakmarian all of a sudden?
q.6216: Ever since I was a kid I was into watchmaking and that's exactly why I chose to worship the god Xelor. Now that I'm better at my hobby, well... it's not longer a hobby. You'll have to come see one of my shows at the arena actually. I'll show you how to make a grown Bworker cry, it's very entertaining. I'm actually talking with Moob Tsinhcetoryp about putting on a pyrotechnics show.
q.9977: I'm not here for honour or glory, ya know. Being a mercenary is just the best way for me to fill my purse with kamas.
q.6231: I was just admiring the rolling countryside from my Imp Carrier when I fell off... I leant too far over the edge. Fortunately a goblin broke my fall. There was nothing left of him but a stinking pile of mush. Then the goblins captured me, but they had too much to carry so they got rid of the Sram they had with them - must have found me more palatable - and, well, you know the rest. As far as I could see they were planning on preparing a feast and I was the main course!
q.6248: You're going to go to the goblin camp and bring this Sram. Just so you can say you haven't come for nothing, here are some potions that might be useful to you in case you get in trouble. If you find the adventure too risky, take some other militiamen with you, that'll give them some exercise and it'll mean I don't have to send them to get you as well as the Sram. Don't bother coming back without information, you know what'll happen to you if you do.
q.6250: That's not what I'm asking you, you little brat. Another comment like that and I'll stretch your tongue so long you'll be able taste farther that you can see.
q.6255: Captain Starky is the chief of the Bontarian cavalry. He's a hot head who has lead devastating charges against us time and again. He would have been an excellent Brakmarian soldier, if he had not decided to side with the losers. I think I'll offer him a job in the militia anyway when Bonta is nothing more than a wasteland.
q.9978:
You the newbie sent by the Disciple? Here, take this cloak. It shows you're a member of our group, and it'll evolve based on your level of commitment.

The more you prove yourself, the more it'll represent your worth.
q.6256: What up with Captain Starky anyway? That wimp doesn't even reach up to my ankle, I'll crush him and his Cheekens, I'll stamp on them, I'll climb on a chair and jump on them until all that's left is bony mud. Then I'll drink the Bontarian Cheeken juice for breakfast, the next day I mean.
q.6302: I'm surprised that someone of your rank even knows such a place exists. I know where it is, but I don't want to share my hard-won information free of charge... we are in Brakmar after all, aren't we. Bring me the soul of a Vampire Master so I can make some Nightmarish Incense and I'll not only tell you where the place is, but I'll even give you a few tips on getting in.
q.6299:
I'm going to get in touch with some lawless bandits east of Amakna. I'll enslave their souls and make unstraying footsoldiers of them. But to do this I need to capture their souls and find the objects required to perform the ritual.
Go capture three dark baker souls, two dark miner souls and two dark smith souls. 
You'll have to find a blue, a yellow and a green Corruptah Stone. Miners can create these stones from raw materials you'll get from alchemists. If they refuse to help you, don't hesitate to give them a whipping... or shove knackis up their nose, they're terrified of that for some reason.
q.6314: I wouldn't say no... and I've just finished my bottle. You really came at the right time! *Hic* What would really make me happy would be a beer from the Bagrutte inn, that always reminds me of the good times. *Hic* Actually, bring me back two.. No, five. Ahh, what they hey, make it ten. That should do it.
q.6321:
For me? Oh thank you. So Amayiro is very happy with my work and he's giving me a bonus? Wow, and I thought I was so over the hill that I was only fit for Piwi taming. 
That's not everything, but I've work to finish and I've to go see Two-fingers to sort out some important things. We've just got some new ore in and the quality is higher than before. The new tools are great too. But it means I can't leave the forge empty so you'll have to get out of here. If you need me for anything, don't bother waiting around, you'll just have to come back later.
q.6348: Well, that's not too bad. I'll be able to make my battle robots with this. You want to know what they do? Do you see me asking you any questions? Well, do you?
q.6359: That's a Bontarian warship, that, no? I didn't have a clue they were on the way. You should go and question Wartella, she should have up-to-date info on what Bontarians ships are on their way here, even if no one seems to be telling me.
q.6375:
Poison, to force Elturt to talk? What a great idea!
If you want to make a Rasputin Cake, you'll need to ask a baker to make you one. You'll need the following:
- 3 Pieces of Pippin Blop
- 2 Cherries
- 1 Bowl
- 1 Scurvion Seed
If you forget the recipe, come back and see me.
q.6378:
In fact, it happened a moment ago and I thank you on his behalf. You helped me so now it's my turn to help you.
Elturt is a very old, very wise turtle. He was thrown into the Amakna sewers when he was very young. After a time spent rubbing shoulders with Sphincter Cell and having defeated Herr Palp Itane in the Cania Marathon of 532 he was swept away by floodwaters during the great flood of 540 and beached on Wabbit Island, which at the time was inhabited by the Lenalds. Having failed to stem the Wabbit invasion, he swam all the way over to Moon Island. There, ashamed of his failure and being different from other turtles, he isolated himself in the deep jungle and has lived as a hermit until now.
They say he has strong powers inherited from his stay in the sewers and that he has sharpened his fighting techniques over the centuries. According to the latest rumours, he could be the guardian of a powerful magic horn but I didn't really pay much attention to them.
q.6384: Eltuwt? That infewnal cweatuwe is still alive? What is this stowy you'd have me believe? I don't want to heaw any mowe about him. He humiliated me and ovew the yeaws, I had to live in shame, and it's all his fault. Today, you'we offewing me the oppowtunity to avenge myself and I find myself unable to help you. Why? Because I'm widdled with awthwitis since the lightning stwuck my fingewtips. It's extwemely painful and debilitating. I can, howevew, tell you his weak spot, if you pwomise to avenge me.
q.6387: Where's my head at? I even forgot to give them back to him the last time we spent the night together... anyway, that doesn't concern you. Here are the keys. Tell him that next time I'll remember to give them back to him before he has to send someone to remind me, he's very grumpy sometimes.
q.6833:
A foul-smelling Sram? Why didn't you say so before? If I answer will you stop boring me with your stories of owls and spelling? Okay.
It doesn't exactly smells like roses here, but I know a Sram who smells worse than a legion of Grossewer Rats. That must be why they let him come and go down the drain as he sees fit, they must think he's one of them.
Usually he descends into the sewers through the entrance to the southeast of the city. His name? Gnirreh. It makes me think of rotten fish.
Now that you've got what you wanted go back to your boss and leave my wife out of it.
q.6411:
You look like you've just soiled yourself. Here, I wrote down the recipe on this piece of paper. Guard it with your life and don't talk to anyone about it or I'll kill you while you sleep.
Since you're here, as you seem to be looking for old recipes, go interrogate my friend Nikos Monot, he knows a good one. Don't, however, listen to his stories as he's a little crazy. He told me stories about the water stretching as far as the eye could see to the west of the Cania Plains and that boats can travel on it for months. Everyone knows that the Cania Plains stretch into infinity.
q.6419: Don't fear me, young adventurer! I can send you to the cemetery ... without taking your meaningless soul from this terrible and dangerous world! Rid the world of all the species living in and I'll send you where they all end up...
q.6422:
You're like a bad smell, you are. Show me your sword.
...
I've seen many Ecaflips with this type of sword. The ones who live outside the city walls. I can't remember where exactly though - do you think I remember everywhere I go, do you? Speaking of going, didn't I ask you to get the hell out of here?
q.6423:
You're like a bad smell, you are. Show me your sword.
...
I've seen many Ecaflips with this type of sword. The ones who live outside the city walls. I can't remember where exactly though - do you think I remember everywhere I go, do you? Speaking of going, didn't I ask you to get the hell out of here? How about I give you a makeover with my fingernails?
q.6437: Hello! My name is Cheeka and I'm the leader of an important group of merchants. When I'm not doing business, I'm doing businessmen and believe me, I know exactly how to mix business with pleasure! They say I'm very stiff when it comes to business, but believe me - they're the ones who are stiff! So what do you think about it?
q.6439: Look now, a strapping warrior like you shouldn't play shy. If you do business with me, I'll soon lighten your purse. That will take some of the weight off your shoulders. Purses are like cups, you must empty them to fill them up anew.
q.6447: Ughhh, you're disgusting! It would be cruel to the Gobball to let you near him, besides, I don't want something I'm going to eat myself to go licking you from top to bottom. Go find me that Sram and make sure that you keep your personal issues to yourself in future. God, just picturing you with a Gobball is disgusting me.
q.6465: Thanks a lot. I sure owe you one. I'll give you some of the synthetic jelly that I invented myself... and the recipe so you can make more. If you're not skilled enough to do it, just ask a handyman to help you out. Let me tell you right now though, that's the last bit of jelly you get off me so just make sure that the handyman who helps you doesn't mess things up!
q.6469: Hello there. So, you're in charge of the supplies? You must have done something really stupid to end up here. Unless you've just joined the militia and Amayiro has chosen a particularly nasty initiation task for you! Whatever the case, thanks for the ham!
q.6485: Very funny. You've got no business here, so go play monkey somewhere else until I give the signal. If I don't pay attention, someone could easily come along and steal the documents... and very likely hurt me too.
q.6488: Ah, it's you? I didn't recognize you with those ridiculous clothes on. Let's go quick, I really don't want anyone to notice us - and I definitely don't want to get put in chains here with so many Tofoones about.
q.6490:
Hahahaha!
HOHOHOHOHOHOHAHA!!
I can smell you from 100 yards, and you dare come ask me for a favour?
HuhuhuhuhHOHOHO!
Give me a sapphire and I'll tell you where the poison is kept. Unless I change my mind in the meantime. 
Hahahaha!
HOHOHOHOHOHOHAHA!!
q.6492: Hello hello. Are you a trader? No? Supplier? Trafficker? No? Hm, well I don't think I've anything for you in that case. I organise convoys to Astrub.
q.6500: Haha! You're even dumber than you look. I just have to snap my fingers and the entire Brakmar militia will come looking for me. So do you feel like taking on forty armed guards at once? No? Well I suggest you learn some manners then. Please and thank you're so old-fashioned... how about 10,000 Kamas or so to lighten the atmosphere?
q.6506: Don't worry, we've caught Xephires. Here, take him to Amayiro yourself, it's thanks to you that we found out about his treason after all. Just try not to let him get away this time.
q.6510:
ahahahahahhaahahah
HAHAHAHAHHARHARHARHHAA!
You're poor, you don't have a coin in your pocket and you think you can survive in Brakmar?
Hahahhahaaahahaaahaha
HARHARHAHARHARHAAHA!
q.6897:
Is that a real Hypnomeow? Unbelievable! It's been years since I've seen one, well, not a live one, anyway.
So you'd like me to train it to take part in interrogations? It'd be a pleasure, it'll be a nice change from training Whitish Fangs.
Tell Ture Inge I'll let him know as soon as the Hypnomeow is ready.
q.6511: A gaming room? I don't know what you... Oh, it's you! I'm sorry, a thousand apologies, I did not want to lie to you. It's just that... I can't talk about it to anyone, you understand? Here's a key so you can go there even if I'm not here, the hidden entrance is at the back of the room. It's always a pleasure to receive a Brakmarian of your rank in our tavern. And look, if you're not too busy, my shift finishes between 21:30 and 22:00...
q.6512: A gaming room? I don't know what you... Oh, it's you! I'm sorry, a thousand apologies, I did not want to lie to you. It's just that... I can't talk about it to anyone, you understand? Here's a key so you can go there even if I'm not here, the hidden entrance is at the back of the room. It's always a pleasure to receive a Brakmarian of your rank in our tavern.
q.6517:
ahahahahahhaahahah
HAHAHAHAHHARHARHARHHAA!
You look like someone who'd appreciate the place, but when I'm there I don't talk shop, so there's no point in keeping on asking. Come and play with us or find yourself another table.
Hahahhahaaahahaaahaha
HARHARHAHARHARHAAHA!
q.6531: I detest these bandits. They're bad for business... especially MY business. We taught them a lesson this time. Thanks for being so... impartial. Show Amayiro this brooch to show him how grateful I am. It's not worth a penny, so he'll probably give it back to me soon enough.
q.9979: I can teach you all existing professions, but only if you do a daily mission.
q.6552: Have you seen the militia's equipment, before you come here insulting me? This runt of an Osamodas got the entire contract! Can you believe that! Latem Sa is his name. He couldn't make so much as a saddle for a Tofu, never mind craft weaponry... You want to know what I think? His father got him the job, he's great friends with the attendant. Ah yes. If you want to find this incompetent fool, he'll be in Astrub, he's doing an apprenticeship there.
q.6558: Work for the army? Never again! I left a few years back, and I'm not about to return now. I set up shop in Amakna so as to have some peace and quiet. There's no trouble here, and no worries. You should do the same before it's too late. What's more, if you're thinking of taking my advice, Amakna militia just recruited a young Iop who would be happy to help you get out of Bonta militia. If you continue on the path you're walking now, I can't do a thing for you, although maybe Otho Laringo will agree to help you. He owns the workshop in the North of the village.
q.6563:
Wow, it's amazing. You guarantee it's never been used? I don't want to catch anything!
I'm finally going to be able to get rid of the old one. No more red raw skin and scabs!
I've to test it again just to make sure you aren't doing one over on me.
q.6588: I don't know any more about it, but I reckon the Sadidas hold a grudge against him still, even after all these centuries. If you really want to find out more, Epuop Tik at the Sadida Temple should be able to help you out. He's a living encyclopedia, he knows everything about everything that concerns his race. If you're really stuck, you can go see the Bwork Mages, but since they often hang out with their less evolved cousins, you'll probably have to smash a few heads in before you even start a conversation.
q.9980: What profession do you want to learn?
q.9966:
You've done it. After all this time, all those trials, you finally made it. Not many people can say the same.

You've reached the highest rank of the mercenaries. It's not just a matter of endurance or skill any more, but proof of your worth. You are a model for whoever follows in your steps.

Along with the title, you get one last privilege: access to the upper level of the mercenaries' residence. Only the greatest are allowed in.

So go and see what's up there for you.
q.6598: What have you done to that doll? Have you seen the state of it? It won't be easy to patch it up... I don't know if it's even possible. Well don't just stand there. Get me 1 Silkworm Cocoon, 1 Costumagus Needle, 5 Trunknid Leaves and 2 Black Gobbly Leathers.
q.6666:
I didn't think your rat face looked familiar. Welcome to the Brakmarian Militia, you'll suffer but your enemies will suffer more. Thank Snori Nairb for me, and tell him he'll be paid as agreed. Actually, don't bother thanking him, just tell him he needs to send me a few more people if he wants to see his purse grow.
Don't forget to come back here, I've a few tasks for you and I don't want to involve any of the other militiamen.
q.6760: Hey zere. I'z really happy to zee you guys, you 'ave changed my life. Sanks to you I won't 'ave to leave my village... I'm eternally grateful. What brings you 'ere anyway?
q.6765: What are you doing here? The god Sadida forbids all creatures but his disciples to come this way, and even they need a good reason, if they don't wish to anger him. I saw Sadida when he was angry once, and I don't want to see it again, and I was only watching... imagine what it was like for the poor souls who annoyed him. It was terrible, I've trouble even thinking of it. I don't want to experience it again, so I advise you to leave this place right now. Of course you can try and convince me that you can't go back because Sadida's magic won't let you out of here... well if that's true, how did you get here in the first place? I didn't see any road signs... maybe you just followed your nose!
q.6783:
Shh, not so loud. This is a library, not the Bagrutte Inn. I can only see four solutions. The first - reunite the six primordial Dofus. With that much power in your hands you'd have no problem releasing the Bwork mage from his unhappy state. 
The second is to invoke the demon of the 666th circle and to make a pact with him. Unfortunately I don't know what such a pact would entail, so you'll have to find him and discuss it with him yourself.
The third solution is to empty the Asse sea in less than three days, which is almost impossible, obviously. The last possibility is a ritual which consists of travelling around the Cania Plains in eighty days on one hand... blindfold. I don't need to tell you that you cannot change hands once you've set off. 
If it comes to it, I suppose you could always try to sort things out by making a clothes peg and... ahhh, sorry, forget what I just said.
q.6806:
According to you, Robin Gaywould will reveal some valuable information to us if we can ensure he and his boars are kept safe?
Well, as the leader of the militia and responsible for the security of this city, I must protect its inhabitants. Go see Red Nefed - he's taking a break in the Woodenglass Inn - and tell him he is now assigned to monitor Robin Gaywould's paddock. Then, return to Robin Gaywould and use your wits to get him to tell you everything he knows about Kit Dingaround and his alleged treason.
q.6847: Thanks...hic...that'sh very kind of yoush. I don't know why, but at the moment...burp...my throat ish alwaysh dry. Hic. Here, for example, I jusht drank a pint...hic...and it'sh ash if I didn't have anything to drink. With that in mind, have you...hic...got a couple of Kamash so I could buy...so I could buy...erm, what wash I shaying? Oh yeah, 'ave you got two Kamas so I can...oh, never mind..
q.6880:
Oh, but isn't mummy's Bow Meow a cutie! Without me, this adorable little animal would have ended up in the belly of a dangerous monster or as a ghost under the blows of a vile butcher's cleaver. But fortunately for him, I'm here and I make sure he has everything he needs.
As an Eniripsa,my skills come in very handy when he's feeling poorly, but I can also repel intruders when they come here. Nobody cares much about his health other than me. He is so cute...
q.6892: I bet you wouldn't last more than five minutes, but it seems that fate willed otherwise. Next time luck will be on my side and you'll end up as black pudding or pâté for my Bow Meow.
q.6929:
The Xelor tile is located in Feudala Village, but I do not know where exactly. I have not set foot there since then and at the time I didn't know the places I do now. Only a disciple of Xelor can use its magic, provided they have equipped a Xelor's Past and are in possession of a Temporal Powder.
If you want to know where the Enutrof tile is, go and talk to Nystig. He moved with his wife to the south of Dragoturkey Territory because he took up hunting and cooking Dragoturkeys.
q.6939:
At a session of frenzied shovel-rolling, my husband told me where to find the tile and how to activate its magic.
He buried it north-east of here, at the foot of a Dragoturkey statue. Only a Enutrof with a Crackler's Golden Tooth in their inventory and wearing an Enutrof's Memento can activate its magic.
If it helps, write down whatever you need to remember the information, and don't forget our deal when you see the medium.
q.6896:
Hahaha, she's a frisky one alright. But you know, not all Iops are idiotic headbangers. Take Helsephine for example. A disciple of Iop and a successful alchemist at once. Ok, I mean, she was only a woman after all, but apart from that she wasn't too bad. 
Men usually like nothing much besides the blood and sweat of the battlefield, but there too you find exceptions. Rish Claymore, now there's a cultured fellow. He might have got where he's through violence, but since he arrived, he's taken up cooking, sewing and tennis, among other refined pastimes. A shining example of Iopness.
q.7008:
To forge a Dontase Mebro Shovel, you'll need to find a shovel smith. Yes, I know, it seems obvious to you, but it isn't for everyone. You must then assemble the following resources: 1 Transmuted Water, 10 Crackler's Golden Teeth, 2 Aluminite, 1 Magnesite and 10 Maple Wood.
I forgot: it is essential that you bring me the shovel's user manual, Dragonsly should have one. Get one when you go see him.
q.7020:
Top o'the mornin' to ya! I'm Sag Dratsum, descendant of the very first Sag the Enutrof.
As you can see there's plenty of work to do here, the place is a real building site. You might wonder what an Enutrof is doing among all these Pandawas, I'll explain in a moment. Us Enutrofs have centuries of experience in the field of drilling. As drilling is my specialty, they hired me to direct operations.
When I arrived it was a real mess here, but since I took things in hand, it's a bit better. Still, be careful not to fall into a hole, you'll have rotten away to nothing before anyone comes to help you.
q.7031:
I expected no less from you. Now listen to me carefully.
The Dawn Shard cannot be forged just anywhere. You'll have to go to the Isle O'Antitch with people you trust. Once there, find a Frozen Crystal to make a Frost Potion. Then, look for a cave cold enough to use the Frost Potion on the Wyrmwell to freeze the water, shatter it, and retrieve the Remembrance Fragments. When this is done, head to the heart of the island with your companions to forge the weapon destined for the great Jiva.
I'm let Kosuke Ichazum know he should join you there.
q.7564:
It's distilled Ouassingue Juice. It's forbidden in all of the world's civilised cities because it causes anyone who drinks it to become hopelessly addicted.
Now you've got what you wanted, go pester someone else.
q.9981: What profession do you want to learn?
q.7072: Salutations! I see you're surprised to be talking to a plant. I suppose you usually take a hoe to creatures like me. Gosh, it's not often you see a warrior with a bit of spirit. As my Root says to me often - How much is between what we think and what we say. I'm not saying anything about what you do, but...
q.7144: You're back from the temple? I hope you took in as much as you could, there's so much to do there.
q.7465: Hello! I can see you've got a Magical Orb. It has two powers but you can only use one of them. Do you want to find out more about them?
q.7468:
If you use this power, all of your characteristics will be reset to zero. You'll lose any points that you gained from characteristic scrolls but you'll get back everything else.
Do you really want to continue?
q.7469:
This power allows you to reset your characteristics to 101, if you don't want to lose anything you've gained through scrolls.
If you use it, any characteristic above the value 101 will be reset to 101, and you'll get back the appropriate number of characteristic points. A characteristic below the value 101 will not be affected.
Do you really want to continue?

q.7587:
Hi! If you're looking to buy a house, you've come to the right place. Thanks to me, you'll have a friend in the estate agent business.
I know what intrigues you, you're wondering who owns this house, that's hidden away in Cania.
q.7613: I can't help you unless you have a Bunch of Keys. To get one, head over to your class temple. You'll win a doploon if you're able to defeat a Dopple in the temple, and you can exchange it for a Bunch of Keys, which will give you free access to all of the dungeons in the game once a week.
q.7615:
Haven't you heard? The two terrible dragons, Grozilla and Grasmera, have been defeated.
You probably don't know what I'm talking about, so let me tell you a little more about them.
q.7616:
Long ago, even before the creation of Xelor's Clock, Crocabulia displeased her master, the god Osamodas. Given a last chance to redeem herself, Crocabulia agreed to watch over a young and fragile new race: the dragons.
To ensure that she carried out her mission, Osamodas entombed the formidable Grozilla and Grasmera in the Sanctuary.
Their first awakening, caused by human folly, was terrible, and heralded the destruction of Amakna's founding village. After the massacre, they returned to the bowels of the earth, hidden away in the Sanctuary. The legends told nothing more of them.
q.7661: So, squirt... This arena's a real knockout, don't you think? I'm so strong that you'll have to submit to my rules here, so listen up. You don't want to see me get angry...¶I'm saying that for everyone's benefit! Heh heh!
q.7617:
Obviously, and that's why I told you you're too late.
Strange Dreggon eggs, nicknamed "Sauroshells", starting appearing all over the peninsula and in the underground during the month of Novamaire in the year 639. Many adventurers and other apprentice Dreggon hunters began looking for them to make omelettes, which were sold for a very high price at King Allister's banquet.
When the last Sauroshell was destroyed, Grozilla and Grasmera came out of their torpor to avenge this irrational destruction.
q.7619:
Show me what you've got there.
Why, it's a Sauroshell fragment!
If you'd like, you can give it to me, and I'll give you a magic amulet in return. Not just any amulet, mind - this amulet will show everyone that you were here when the battle took place.
q.7620:
But... that giant fang that you've got there comes from the jaw of one of the two dragons, doesn't it?
It's enormous! I've never seen one as big. It must make people jealous...
If you like, you can give it to me. I'll give you a shield fashioned from one of Grozilla's scales in return, so that everyone will see how mighty your deeds were.
q.7678:
*A very powerful force looms before you. It is the last obstacle between you and the ruler of this place. 
It is almost certain that forcing your way past will leave you exhausted. 
 
Perhaps there's something that could protect you...*

q.7662: Cheap shots aren't allowed here, pipsqueak: only real warriors deserve to fight under my watch. So while you're getting ready for the fight, you won't be able to see your opponents. You must rely on your instinct.¶ ¶The conflict between Bonta and Brakmar is of no interest to me... Attacking is strictly forbidden in my arena! All right! Since I'm so generous, just this once, I'll allow you to carry a shield of your choice without any restrictions.¶If that's too much for your sensitive eyes, you can always go back to Tainela: they're always looking for people to hit Gobballs! Hahaha...
q.7668:
Hi! 
Looking for fine possessions and fortune? Come on over, I've got a couple of very valuable paddocks here! At great prices, too! And of course they're all up to code, not a single hidden flaw in any one of 'em! 
 
But as a fan of epic battles, I'm only offering them to those who truly deserve them, so get a few allies together and show me what you're made of!
q.7671:
With these potions, you'll temporarily take the form of a variant of your chosen creature: 
The Bworker, an powerful and agile fighter. 
The Skeunk, a magician who can improve and heal their allies. 
And Lord Crow – he's very tough, and can position both allies and enemies however he likes.  
 
 
(TO QUALIFY FOR THE EVENT, YOU MUST BE AT LEAST LEVEL 50 AND PARTICIPATE WITH MEMBERS FROM THE SAME GUILD. MORE INFORMATION AVAILABLE ON THE SITE.)
q.7670:
First of all, let me just warn you that I'll be very strict with my rules. One paw out of place and you'll be disqualified on the spot! 
 
Before sending you into my... arena, I'm going to ask you to choose one of the three potions in front of you, specially designed by Otomai himself!
q.7672:
With these potions, you'll temporarily take the form of a variant of your chosen creature: 
The Bworker, an powerful and agile fighter. 
The Skeunk, a magician who can improve and heal their allies.

q.7680:
But... What's this? 
 
*he stares at the shard in your hand, gazes at you and then worriedly opens his eyes wide* 
 
No! This fragment doesn't bode well... As soon as they appear, it means Grozilla and Grasmera are regaining strength! 
What'll happen if other reckless adventurers like you keep breaking these sauroshells? I don't dare imagine...
q.7866:
Hello, my name is Ennu Prof. Eccentric scholar, misunderstood genius, and of course, a humble scientist. Looking at you, I suspect you think I'm looking for some tough, muscular types to assist me. And while that's true... I'm sorry to say that you don't meet my criteria.  
 
Come back in a few years, once you've built up more experience than a freshly hatched larva.
q.7867: Hello, my name is Ennu Prof. Eccentric scholar, misunderstood genius, and of course, a humble scientist. I was once one of Otomai's disciples, but I eventually decided to strike out on my own. I found that his methods were too focused on preservation. After a few years of stagnation and boredom with him, I realised that all that really counts is the result, regardless of the cost.
q.7868:
What?! 
You've really never heard of me? Me, the inventor of the incredible thyme machine and the amazing intangible fence?! 
 
Of course, all that was long ago... As you can see, I'm now far away from my familiar lab environment. I know all about machines and devices, but I was told that this vast plain might turn out to be a very rewarding place for wildlife research...
q.7876:
Hmph... not very clever, are you?  
Ah, well! You'll change your mind eventually. In the meantime, I'll keep studying this Trool Burger. It's far more interesting than you anyhow.
q.7903:
The plain cards are enough for my research, but I've heard there's someone out there looking for an adventurer who's bold enough to build the finest possible collection... 
Perhaps they're even offering a reward?
q.7869:
Well, you see, I'm always thinking about my next great invention, but despite my immense knowledge, I must admit that I'm a bit in the dark when it comes to living creatures.  
 
Now don't look at me like that; I can't be expected to know everything!  
 
Still, I'll bet you didn't know that the reason a Kilibriss is always clinging to a branch is because they're afraid of deep water. That way, even if they jump into the surf at low tide, they stay dry. Almost as ingenious as something I might have invented.
q.7871: Ah, you see: I was right! Still, it's admirable that you've at least got the decency to admit it.
q.7870: Don't lie to me; I can tell when someone's fibbing! And in this case, that someone is you.
q.7874: Each card represents a creature in the same level of detail as if you had it right there in front of you. With these cards, I'll be able to study them without having to traipse up hill and down dale. Needless to say, you'll be handsomely rewarded.
q.7873: That's just because you haven't been paying attention. I'm sure you'll look more carefully from now on.
q.7879: Once you've beaten a creature in combat, there's a chance you'll find a pack of cards on its body. Open it up, and you've got yourself a card for that family. If it's a card you've already got, then it's up to you whether to sell it, trade it or recycle it.
q.7880:
Ah, very observant of you! Excellent! These are two masterpieces of my own creation. The magic table and the card recycler! 
 
You can use the magic table to merge three copies of the same card into a shiny "foil" version. The really clever thing about this table is, it can detect and use a card that's already in your binder, so you just need to add two more copies after that. Then it takes the resulting foil card and puts it right back into your binder. 
 
I've heard there's someone out there looking for an adventurer who's pulled off the achievement of filling in the entire binder that way... but I've no idea who that might be.
q.7881:
The recycler is another extraordinary machine that'll help you fill up your binder. I'll spare you the technical details, but basically, it grinds your cards down to dust and reconstitutes them into a new pack. The more rare cards you put in it, the better the chances that its magic will work.  
 
Absolutely brilliant, isn't it? Please, there's no need for compliments; I know I'm a genius.
q.7895:
Yes, you're right. That was another adventurer whom I'd asked to help me with my research. He introduced himself not long before you arrived, but it seems I misjudged him. What a sneaky, devious person! I can hardly believe it! Was he motivated by jealousy, or some darker design? 
 
 
... 
 
 
Perhaps... yes, of course! It may not be too late!
q.7896: Take this Tabi. It's a rare creature that I managed to tame before arriving in Cania. He's incredibly fleet-footed, so I'm sure with his help you'll be able to catch up to that bandit!
q.7899:
On second thoughts, you look tough. No point losing my teeth for these old bits of paper. Look... go on and keep your old binder; I don't want it anymore. But you tell that Ennu he's a stingy old bugger. 
 
*throws the binder on the ground and guzzles a purplish potion*
q.7897:
*gasping for breath* 
You... you've caught me... That old geezer lent you his mount...  
Bah... I should've... thought of that... before running off... on foot... 
 
*catches his breath* 
Oh well, no matter. En garde!
q.7901:
No, I don't think it'd be fair to take it back after all that's happened. Besides, it seems to have taken a liking to you, and I think it needs to stretch its legs like that more often.  
 
I have an idea! Why not take it with you on your adventures?
q.7907:
My colleague Gladiatrade just outside will be happy to take whatever gladiokens you've earned and trade you all sorts of prizes for them. The most courageous, or the luckiest, will earn a medal if they manage to win it all... and that medal will give you access to some prestigious rewards. 
 
The further you progress in the Gladiatrool challenge, the more tokens you'll get at the end of a fight. But be careful: losing a fight means you'll lose all the tokens you've earned in your current session. If you don't think you can beat the group you're up against, come and talk to me to bail out and cash in your winnings.
q.7914:
Talk about a crushing victory! Magnificent! 
 
You've definitely earned this medal, these 1,250 tokens and this bonus! Come back any time you want to take another shot at the Gladiatrool challenge!
q.9604: Nice fight! The question now is: will you continue to fight, or stop now? Note that you've collected 70 tokens so far.
q.9603: Nice fight! The question now is: will you continue to fight, or stop now? Note that you've collected 30 tokens so far.
q.7920:
Oooh! Finally, a worthy opponent. Our battle will be legendary. 
 
En garde!
q.9640: I toss a kama to decide who will start... Tails! That means it's my turn to play. I draw a card and summon the "Immature Golden Dreggon". I finish by placing a card face down. Now it's your turn. Try and defeat me.
q.9965:
You're back. It's becoming obvious that you take your commitments seriously.

As a reward for your perseverance, you can now enter the mercenaries' residence.

You can use our secret passage to get there faster.
q.9644:
My turn to draw a card... By Ecaflip! It seems like luck is on my side. I start by playing the ""Osamodas's Whip"" card, which lets me remove a creature of my choice from the field, and I destroy your card. 

Then I sacrifice my ""Immature Golden Dreggon"" and summon my all-powerful ""Black-Eyed Golden Dragoone""!

Using the ""Advantageous Roulette"" card, I make you skip a turn, and I attack with my Dragoone. Just as I thought, you weren't up to it...""
q.9883: ... Lieutenant As'Ruoy'Dnim, Qu'Tan, is still kicking himself for letting you get away with his Ebony Dofus...
q.9870: Are you surprised I know your name? No secret is safe from the watchful eye of Jack! Your fate, young adventurer, is mapped out... and I can share it with you if you like.
q.9877: ... You brought down the dreaded Dark Vlad and got his Emerald Dofus...
q.9885: ... You still have some way to go, but that doesn't mean you can't fulfil your duty. That of restoring the fragments' radiance...
q.9882:
... The fearsome Crocabulia, mother to Crocoburio, failed to protect the Vulbis Dofus? 



That's... amazing...
q.9887: When the demon As'Ruoy'Dnim invaded Amakna with his henchmen to take the precious Dofus eggs, meteors rained down on Crackler Mountain. In their curiosity, many people went to see what had happened, and they discovered those fragments. Thinking that they were in some way related to the demons, the Amaknians hid them. I found some in my cellar about a decade ago and began studying them.
q.9889: A large number of souls will be needed to restore their radiance. Near their respective Dofus, they're able to absorb a being's life energy right before it goes away to Externam.
q.9888:
See this container next to me? At first blush, it seems like a tourist attraction built to perpetuate the rumour that its potential could be awakened in Pandala. 



But that isn't the case... The fragments really do resonate with the statue. Sadly, however, the fragments' magic has long since been dampened.
q.9891: #1, choose a fragment, and I'll hand it over, but only if you show me the corresponding Dofus.
q.9892: Hmm... No, I don't think it's a good idea. You don't yet have what it takes to go up against these creatures.
q.9890:
If you bring me a fragment brimming with souls, I'll pray at the container on your behalf so as to reimbue it with magic.



Complete the achievement with all six fragments, and perhaps an item with a divine aura will become available...
q.9909:
Equipped with the six Primordial Dofus, this shield can then absorb souls. With that done, it will become a key ingredient in crafting the legendary item that will enable you to rise above your kind.



I'm the owner of the shield, so I'll let you guess what kind of souls are drawn to it...
q.9917:
Perfect.



This is where we part ways, #1. I was destined to cross your path, to guide the true keeper of the Dofusteuse. 

With that accomplished, I can finally go and rest with my loved ones. 



Farewell, #1.
q.9925: ... You didn't get your hands on the Ochre Dofus...
q.9926: ... You didn't get your hands on the Ivory Dofus...
q.9931: Sharp eye, mate! I managed to take 'em down with a swift pitchfork. Heh heh! That's when the orb came outta the pumpkwin mash! But it vanished before I could grab it.
q.9938: Yer not gonna believe this one! The only day of the year that the Drunken Pandawa was shut, I took me raft over to Nolifis Island. I felt so bad... I was going through cold dragoturkey – no bamboo milk, see? But, at that very moment... In the midst of the mist and ectoplasm, I got an eyeful of a strange island! Nobody had seen it before! It must've been under a powerful camouflage spell! Or the fact that nobody's been sober on this island for ages, or I'm not a Pandawa! *burps fervently*
q.9939: Huh, drunk already? Shall we go aboard? I'm a leeetle tipsy, though. *hic*
q.9940: Hey, kid! Came here with the captain, did ye? Yer welcome to enter the sanctuary, but not for free. See, dodging isn't really my bag, and the Nolifishields in stock are vanishing faster than snow in the sunshine with all the ghosts about. Get me one, and I'll let you in; otherwise, clear off! We've found the island; now we're the ones haggling.
q.9941: Welcome to my humble tomb. So you're looking to shuffle off this mortal coil sooner than expected? Well, it's your funeral. Go ahead – choose whichever path you like. The same fate awaits you, whichever way you go...
q.9942: Hmm, you're better than I thought. Just so you know, behind me, you'll find the dungeon keeper, if you want to go and tussle with them directly. But that's likely to end up with you getting trounced by all the elemental masters you haven't beaten yet who'll come flocking. Anyway, as soon as you think you're ready to battle their leader, just let me know. Take your time; I've got all eternity in front of me...
q.7906:
Each session is made up of 10 challenges of increasing difficulty. The further you go, the more challenging it gets. But don't worry: after each fight you win, you'll be able to choose a tonic that'll give you a permanent bonus for the rest of your session and make you more powerful for the challenges ahead. 
 
One more important detail: whether you fight alone or with an ally, the difficulty remains the same. So I'd recommend finding an ally... unless you're feeling especially lucky!
q.9955:
Me, single? Seriously? Hahaha!

I haven't heard that one in a looooong time! Just ask my mates if I'm seeing anyone... Like, last week I was on this wild date... so heyyyy, take it easy!

'Cause you seem like you've got limited experience in that area. People like you tend to get frustrated over not having much of a love life.
q.9953:
I was just undercover in a top-secret mission given by the Rogue brotherhood, which was in a pretty strange dimension... The furniture was modern, and the people were all dressed the same and had no weapons. They'd meet in closed rooms and chat for hours. Different customs, I suppose.

Now that mission is complete, I'm back in the World of Twelve to do what I really enjoy: watch fights, see teeth flying, give commentary on the whole thing – in a spirit of healthy competition, mind you.

I've brought back bits and baubles from my travels – but I'll only trade them to those who prove their mettle in combat. That could be you!
q.9952:
Hello and welcome to the arena! Pantalemon, Rogue disciple at your service... especially if you're the highest bidder.

If you've got champion brooches, come and see me: I'll take them in exchange for prizes you won't find anywhere else. I already have quite the collection, but nowhere near enough for my liking.

Good luck out there, and let's keep it a clean fight!
q.2449: Hello, brave adventurer. Welcome to our humble home. We are a clan of noble mercenaries, devoted to the people. We take care of all sorts of things. For a few Kamas, we'll help you find that item you've been looking for, we'll accompany you in your dangerous adventures... you want someone killed? We can do that too... Please come inside if you want to meet our clan. You can join us if you like, just contact the clan master.
q.9971: Every mission has a price. The real question is: is it worth the risk?
q.6594: Hello there. I organise unusual tracking expeditions with another member of my family. If you'd like to come along with us some time, just let me know. I'll give you a target to catch and if you succeed I'll pay you for it. But I don't want any cowards or glory-hunters on my team. Any fights you fight will be fair and honourable. It's not always easy to find an even match, but the minute I've something for you, I'll give you Seeker scrolls to help you. So, are you ready?
q.9968: Our chief asked me to give you this as a reward for your involvement. And you've ranked up.
q.9958:
There you are, #1, just in time. Someone in the World of Twelve needs help, and I think you can handle it.

If you accept this mission, you'll be rewarded. And your commitment won't go unnoticed: by completing multiple missions, you can get even better rewards.

So, mercenary, are you ready to dive in?
q.9959: So, have you advanced in your quest?
q.9962:
Ah, you're new. Good, we could always use motivated mercenaries. You might run into a few obstacles, but it's a chance to show what you're made of.

Only those who really get involved earn a place here. Prove yourself, and you'll see that your commitment won't go unnoticed.

So, mercenary, ready to dive in?
q.9963:
You did pretty well. Clearly you aren't just a fly on the wall.

As a reward for your hard work in the mercenary clan, you can now access the upper level. Keep it up.

Someone's expecting you inside.
q.9964:
Ah, there you are. Always around, that's good.

You've been promoted! The boss is giving you access to the lower level.

You can go in; someone's waiting for you.
q.9967:
That's a good start.

To reward your joining the mercenary clan, we're giving you a privilege: access to the ground floor of the mercenaries' residence. Consider it a first step. But don't get too comfortable. You've still got a long way to go.

Someone's expecting you inside.
q.9969: One day, I'll be known all across the World of Twelve! For now, I'm taking things as they come, but just you wait...
q.9970: Here, take this sword. It's been in quite a few battles, but it'll still get the job done in the right hands.
q.9972: I heard you could use a travelling companion. Good timing – that little one happens to need an owner.
q.9973: Also, there's a secret passage right here, behind these crates. You can use it as a way out of the Cania Plains. Don't tell anyone about this – it could save your life some day.
q.9974: You seem like the type to charge in... Here, take this shield. It might just keep you getting crushed too fast.
